questions.question: A PDA's stack can hold at MOST 5 symbols at any time (hard-capped). What class of languages does it accept?
questions.solutionApproach: A stack capped at a CONSTANT size has only finitely many possible contents — this collapses to a finite number of distinguishable 'configurations', same power as a finite automaton. Class = Regular.
questions.answer: Regular — bounded stack size collapses PDA power to finite-automaton power.

questions.question: L1 = {a^n b^n c^m : n,m≥0} (CFL). L2 = {a^m b^n c^n : n,m≥0} (CFL). Is L1∩L2 guaranteed CFL?
questions.solutionApproach: No — CFL∩CFL has NO general guarantee. L1∩L2 = {a^n b^n c^n} which is CONTEXT-SENSITIVE, not CFL. This is the classic demonstration of CFL's non-closure under intersection, now viewed through the hierarchy lens.
questions.answer: No — L1∩L2 = {a^n b^n c^n}, which escapes CFL entirely into context-sensitive territory.

questions.question: L is Recursively Enumerable but NOT Recursive. Is complement(L) Recursively Enumerable?
questions.solutionApproach: No — this is the exact boundary case. If BOTH L and complement(L) were RE, then L would be Recursive (a known theorem: L is Recursive iff both L and complement(L) are RE). Since L is RE-but-not-Recursive, complement(L) CANNOT be RE.
questions.answer: No — complement(L) is NOT RE (otherwise L would be Recursive, contradiction).

questions.question: Classify L = {a^n b^n c^n : n≥0}.
questions.solutionApproach: Not regular (unbounded matching), not CFL (needs 3-way simultaneous matching, single stack insufficient — provable via CFL pumping lemma). It IS context-sensitive (a linear-bounded automaton can verify it) and Recursive (decidable — an algorithm can always check and halt).
questions.answer: Context-Sensitive (and Recursive), but NOT Context-Free and NOT Regular.
